sections.h2: What should I know before selling a house in North Lauderdale?
sections.html:
North Lauderdale is a Broward County city that grew from farmland into a mostly residential community, and a quirk of its rules matters to sellers: the city requires an inspection and a residential rental license before an owner may offer a home for rent. If the buyer is an investor who plans to rent, or if you rented the house yourself, that rule comes up quickly.

The city's fire department history says North Lauderdale was 90 percent farmland when it incorporated in 1963. A handful of early residents shared fire service with neighboring Margate and the Bailey Road Volunteer Fire Department, and in 1973 officials authorized a volunteer department with a station on Rock Island Road.

That history explains why housing here dates mostly from the decades after incorporation, so roofs, wiring and air conditioning are the items buyers tend to question.

sections.h2: How did annexation and growth shape North Lauderdale?
sections.html:
The 2004 annexation of the Broadview and Pompano Park area added about 12,000 residents, the busy State Road 7 corridor and a new fire station, according to the city's fire rescue history. That annexation matters to a seller because a few neighborhoods were unincorporated county land until then, so their records and permits may sit with either Broward County or the city.

  • Station 44, begun in 1991, sits near the middle of the city.
  • Station 34, finished in 2008, serves the east side and carries the name of the city's first city clerk.
  • The department became a full-service fire and EMS department in 2002 and now lists more than 40 firefighter-paramedics.

The page also notes mutual aid agreements with Broward County and adjacent cities, which is the arrangement behind emergency coverage across the area.

sections.h2: What does North Lauderdale require for a rental property?
sections.html:
The city's business tax receipt page says no one may offer residential units for rent unless the building has been inspected by the community development department and the owner of record holds a residential rental license, which is a local business tax receipt. A buyer who plans to rent the house must plan for that step.

Residential rental license charges printed on the North Lauderdale business tax receipt page

Single-family$32$63.60

The same page lists a $65 initial application fee, a business tax receipt fee of $11.60 per unit and a $20 renewal fee. Because those figures come from an older notice on the page, ask the city for the current schedule. If you do not receive rent on the property, the city provides an affidavit of no residential rental compensation.

sections.h2: What inspection standards could a North Lauderdale rental inspection check?
sections.html:
The city lists standards for exterior, interior and outside property conditions. Passing them is a requirement for the rental license, and an investor buyer will apply the same checklist to your house.

  • Exterior walls must be kept free of holes and loose boards, and repainted when 25 percent or more of an exposure is discolored or peeling.
  • Roofing and guttering must keep water out, and windows and doors must be weather tight.
  • Electrical wiring, plumbing and heating and ventilation must be in safe working condition.
  • Pools and patios must be clean and screened enclosures intact.
  • Storm water must drain without running onto other properties.

Fixing a few of these items before you list can speed a sale, since a buyer who sees an easy rental inspection is more likely to offer without a long repair negotiation.

sections.h2: What Florida tax and closing rules apply in North Lauderdale?
sections.html:
Deeds in Broward County carry the standard 70 cents per $100 documentary stamp rate, paid to the clerk at recording. The state says every party is liable regardless of which one agrees to pay, so the sales contract should assign it.

  • Property is assessed each January 1 and homestead applications are due by March 1.
  • The Notice of Proposed Property Taxes arrives in August and a petition is due within 25 days.
  • Bills go out in November, discounts shrink from 4 percent to 1 percent by February, and April 1 begins delinquency.
  • A sale resets a homesteaded assessment to just value on the next January 1.

The Broward County Property Appraiser handles exemptions, and the City of Miramar's tax page lists their customer service line as 954-357-6830, a number that applies countywide for exemption questions.

sections.h2: What are the ways to sell a North Lauderdale house quickly?
sections.html:
Sellers here usually weigh a listing against a direct sale to an investor. A listing may bring a higher price from a financed buyer but needs showings, an appraisal and repairs. A cash sale shortens the timeline and often lets the buyer take on a rental license and repairs, with the price reflecting that.

If you are behind on the mortgage, Florida requires the court to enter a final judgment before the clerk's public sale, which then happens 20 to 35 days later unless the lender allows more time. If an heir needs to sell, summary administration may apply to estates of $150,000 or less, and creditors have until the later of three months after notice publication or 30 days after service to file claims.

Compare written offers, ask who pays title and doc stamps, and keep the buyer's rental license plans in the conversation.

faqs.q: Do I need a rental license to sell a North Lauderdale house?
faqs.a: No, the license is for owners who offer units for rent. If you rented the house, ask the city about any open inspection or license issues before closing.
In 1963, according to the city's fire rescue history, which says the area was 90 percent farmland at the time.
About 12,000 residents, the State Road 7 corridor and a new fire station, per the fire rescue history. The area had been unincorporated Broward County.

faqs.q: Where can a buyer file a business tax receipt application?
faqs.a: At North Lauderdale City Hall at 701 SW 71 Avenue, where the city says applications and fees are processed. The business tax receipts line is 954-724-7069.

faqs.q: Does the Florida deed tax change in Broward County?
faqs.a: No. Broward uses the standard 70 cents per $100 of consideration, paid at recording by the clerk, and all parties to the deed are liable.
